text:
anya: quick update — ran the actnorm + SmoothQuant hybrid (we're calling it actnorm-sq-hybrid) across the 60k longspan suite. posting numbers and config.

anya: TL;DR: AWQ-int8 baseline -> +0.8% avg bleu drop; actnorm-sq-hybrid (mixed FP8/INT8 placement) reduces average quality delta to +0.12%, 2.3% p95 latency improvement vs FP8-only. KV-cache eviction still the main tail pain at 60k.

mike: nice. which model/version? and what's the eval set? :eyes:

anya: model: redwood/open-13b-v2 (serving-2026-02-18). eval: longspan-kvbench-60k (mix of code/docs/conversations), 1k samples.

anya: config snippet:
```
quant_strategy: hybrid
placement:
  layers_fp8: [0-3, 48-51]  # keep first/last blocks in FP8
  layers_int8: [4-47]
awq_params:
  group_size: 128
  actnorm_calib: true
runtime:
  kv_cache: enabled
  kv_eviction_policy: lru_threshold=0.85
```

dario: how did you do actnorm calibration? per-layer or global? did you re-run activation collection on 60k sequences?

anya: per-layer actnorm. calibration run on 10k sequences sampled from the 60k suite (randomly stratified by length). used 32-bit activations during collection.

sophia: numbers pls (latency / quality / mem)

anya: paste of core metrics (relative to FP16 full-precision):
- FP8-only (baseline): mean bleu -0.9%, p50 latency +12%, p95 latency +35%, GPU mem -38%
- AWQ-int8 baseline: mean bleu -1.2%, p50 latency +6%, p95 +22%, mem -45%
- actnorm-sq-hybrid: mean bleu -0.03%, p50 latency -2.3% (vs AWQ-int8), p95 latency +16% (vs FP16), mem -40%
- inference throughput (tokens/s) improved ~8% vs AWQ-int8 on 80k batch horizon.

luca: that's surprisingly small quality hit. any examples where it breaks? longer code completions?

anya: yes — we saw focused regressions on long code generation where function signatures depend on subtle activation scale. about 15 samples had notable token-level perplexity spikes. tagging them as "actnorm-sq-outliers" in the test harness.

mike: did you try alternate KV eviction (time-based or half-life caching) to address p95?

anya: tried time-based TTL=30s, reduced p95 by ~4% but increased mem pressure. overall sweet spot seems lru_threshold=0.9 + small batch size tuning.

dario: what about rollout strategy? can we canary to dedicated first?

anya: plan: canary to Dedicated GPU pool with 10% traffic, monitor rerank/Evals for 24h. fallback policy: auto-fallback to AWQ-int8 if eval BLEU drops >0.5% over baseline or error rate >0.2%.

sophia: add checks for function-call fidelity + code unit tests. also hook Redwood Optimize to suggest batch size tweaks automatically.

anya: good call. will add the function-call eval and enable Optimize suggestions in the canary.

ci-bot: benchmark run completed — 2298800000-run-60k-hybrid-candidate — artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/2298800000/ (logs, golden-diffs, samples)

luca: can you upload the 15 outliers to the thread? i'll take a look tonight.

anya: uploaded diffs to the artifacts + linked 3 representative examples below.

anya: next steps: (1) widen calibration to 25k sequences to see if outliers shrink, (2) test TTL vs LRU with controlled mem cap, (3) run 48h canary on Dedicated with rollback hooks.

mike: sg. can you open a short runbook for the canary including rollback commands? e.g.,
```
# rollback snippet
redwoodctl deploy rollback --service=open-13b-v2 --target=awq-int8
redwoodctl traffic set --pool=dedicated --percent=0
```

anya: will add a runbook and link in the canary PR. thanks all :rocket:

sophia: love it, great work. when you open the PR ping eng-oncall and infra for possible memory tuning.

anya: will do. ping me for any quick checks.

ci-bot: note: artifacts retention 14 days.
